text: This is what the LORD says: Where is the certificate of divorce by which I sent your mother away? Or to which of my creditors did I sell you? No — it was for your own sins that you were sold, and for your transgressions that your mother was sent away.

Why was there no one there when I came? Why did no one answer when I called? Is my arm too short to redeem? Do I lack the strength to rescue? Look, at my rebuke I dry up the sea; I turn rivers into desert. Their fish rot for want of water and die of thirst.

versions.text: Why was there no one there when I came? Why did no one answer when I called? Is my arm too short to redeem? Do I lack the strength to rescue? Look, with a single rebuke I dry up the sea; I turn rivers into desert. Their fish rot for want of water and die of thirst.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew בְּגַעֲרָתִי is simply "at/by my rebuke"; the word "single" is an addition not present in the text. "at my rebuke" preserves the meaning without adding an interpretive emphasis, and reads just as well aloud.

text: I clothe the heavens in darkness and wrap them in sackcloth.
The Lord GOD has given me a well-taught tongue, so that I know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens me, he wakens my ear to listen like one who is taught.
The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I did not draw back.
I offered my back to those who struck me, my cheeks to those who tore out my beard. I did not hide my face from insult and spitting.
But the Lord GOD helps me; therefore I am not disgraced. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
The one who vindicates me is near. Who dares to bring a charge against me? Let us confront each other. Who is my accuser? Let him come forward.
See, the Lord GOD helps me. Who then will condemn me? Look, they will all wear out like a garment; the moth will devour them.
Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Whoever walks in darkness with no light at all, let him trust in the name of the LORD and lean on his God.

Look, all of you who kindle a fire and arm yourselves with firebrands: walk by the light of your own fire, by the brands you have set ablaze. This is what you will receive from my hand: you will lie down in torment.

versions.text: But all of you who kindle a fire and arm yourselves with firebrands: walk by the light of your own fire, by the brands you have set ablaze. This is what you will receive from my hand: you will lie down in torment.
versions.explanation: הֵן is the same attention-marker rendered "Look/See" in verses 2 and 9; rendering it as "But" turns a presentative particle into a contrastive conjunction and loses the rhetorical parallel with the preceding verses.
